sla_negotiation_summary: Celestis requires a dedicated SLA negotiation covering: 99.95% monthly uptime target (target), tiered credit schedule (see below), maintenance windows limited to <= 2 hours/month with 72h advance notice, emergency maintenance only with phone escalation and credits applied, P1 support response <= 15 minutes (phone + ticket), P2 <= 1 hour, P3 <= 24 hours. Contract asked for an explicit monthly credit table: <= 99.95% to 99.9% => 5% invoice credit; 99.9% to 99.0% => 15% credit; <99.0% => 50% credit up to 3x months billing cap. Also asked to cap vendor liability to monthly fees and require root-cause reporting within 72 hours of incidents.
throughput_requirements: Interactive chat workload: sustained 1,200 requests/minute during peak with 80 concurrent interactive sessions; batch re-ranking job: 200k documents/night (window 3am-6am). Planning reserved capacity: initial commit for 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or quantized CPU equivalent) with ability to burst +25% for 2 hours/day. Want autoscale burst to use 'burst buffer' credits, pricing unknown.
latency_slos: Interactive target: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms for 2k token contexts on dedicated inference path. For embeddings pipeline p95 < 300ms. Require per-route p50/p95/p99 reporting, and 15-day retention for latency histograms in console.
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial reserved SKU: 8 x H100-equivalent (or Redwood-provided 8x reserved slots). Commit period: 12 months, with optional quarterly review to add capacity. Contract requests explicit inventory reservation guarantees (no reallocation) and 2-week notice for capacity scaling. Want clear definition of 'reserved' vs 'burst' and billing for unused reserved capacity (80% utilization credit?) — negotiation ongoing.
poc_plan: Week 1: Baseline metrics collection — replay 72 hours of traffic to measure latencies and token costs
